These writeups are mathematical companions to the executable chapters in the longitudinal R manual. They emphasize estimands, assumptions, estimation, inference, and interpretation. They do not reproduce code.

## Citation convention

`slide N` is the slide number printed in the lower-left corner of the named lecture deck. It is independent of PDF pagination and therefore remains stable across clean and annotated copies. For supplementary documents without slide footers, `document p. N` denotes the visible document page number. A source note identifies the slides or document pages supporting the immediately preceding result. Proofs are omitted; their source locations are given where available.

## Notation

Subjects or independent clusters are indexed by $i=1,\ldots,N$; repeated observations within subject $i$ are indexed by $j=1,\ldots,n_i$. Unless stated otherwise,

$$
Y_i=(Y_{i1},\ldots,Y_{in_i})^\mathsf T,\qquad
\mu_i=E(Y_i\mid X_i),\qquad
V_i=\operatorname{Var}(Y_i\mid X_i).
$$

The parameter $\beta$ governs the mean model. Parameters $\theta$, $\alpha$, $D$, $R_i$, and $\phi$ govern covariance, association, random effects, or dispersion as defined in each writeup. Independent subjects are the asymptotic sampling units.

## Model-selection decision

For a non-Gaussian longitudinal outcome, the scientific estimand determines the primary model:

$$
\begin{array}{lll}
\text{Marginal/GEE:} & g\{E(Y_{ij}\mid X_{ij})\}=X_{ij}^\mathsf T\beta_{\mathrm{PA}},
& \text{population-average effect};\\[2mm]
\text{GLMM:} & g\{E(Y_{ij}\mid X_{ij},b_i)\}=X_{ij}^\mathsf T\beta_{\mathrm{SS}}+Z_{ij}^\mathsf Tb_i,
& \text{subject-specific effect};\\[2mm]
\text{Transition:} & g\{E(Y_{ij}\mid H_{ij},X_{ij})\}=X_{ij}^\mathsf T\beta_{\mathrm{TR}}+h(H_{ij}),
& \text{effect conditional on response history}.
\end{array}
$$

With a nonlinear link, these parameters generally differ. With a Gaussian identity-link model and $E(b_i)=0$, the fixed effects have both marginal and conditional mean interpretations. *Slide source: `BIOS-767-Part-022.pdf`, slides 25-35; `BIOS-767-Part-010.pdf`, slides 65-69.*

## External cross-checks

The formulations were cross-checked against the primary literature: [Laird and Ware (1982)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7168798/) for LMMs, [Liang and Zeger (1986)](https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/73.1.13) for GEE, [Zeger, Liang, and Albert (1988)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3233245/) for population-averaged versus subject-specific models, [Rubin (1976)](https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/63.3.581) for ignorability, and [Dempster, Laird, and Rubin (1977)](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1977.tb01600.x) for EM.
